exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Gestures Around the World
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Tom, I made the "OK" sign to a waiter in France and he looked upset. Why?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ah, in France that sign can mean zero, or "worthless". It's easy to get wrong.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Really? At home it just means everything is fine.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yes, but the same gesture differs from country to country.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: So what should I do when I travel?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Watch the local people and avoid making gestures you're not sure about.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: That's good advice. I'll be more careful next time.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Don't worry. Everyone makes mistakes like this when learning about a new culture.

exercises.translation_cn: Mia 在法国对服务员比"OK"手势,对方不高兴;Tom 解释在法国那手势可能表示零或"没价值";同一手势因国家而异;Tom 建议旅行时观察当地人、不确定的手势就别比;Mia 表示以后会更小心。

questions.stem: What did the "OK" sign seem to mean in France?
Why did the waiter look upset?
options: He understood the rude meaning of the sign.
He could not find the table.
Mia did not pay the bill.

questions.stem: What does Tom say about the same gesture?
options: It differs from country to country.
It has no meaning at all.

questions.stem: What advice does Tom give for travelling?
options: Watch local people and avoid unsure gestures.

questions.stem: How does Tom make Mia feel better?
options: He tells her to go home.
He says everyone makes such mistakes when learning a culture.
He says France is a bad place.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 The Power of a Smile
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: A smile may be the most powerful piece of body language we have.
It can help us get through difficult moments and find friends among strangers.
We use a smile to greet people, to apologise, or to ask for help.
A warm smile can even break down barriers that words cannot.
So if you feel down, try smiling, and you may slowly feel better.
exercises.translation_cn: 微笑也许是我们最有力的肢体语言;它能帮我们度过难关、在陌生人中找到朋友;我们用微笑问候、道歉或求助;温暖的微笑甚至能打破言语打不破的隔阂;心情低落时不妨微笑,你会慢慢好起来。

questions.stem: What does the speaker call a smile?
options: The most powerful piece of body language.

questions.stem: What can a smile help us do in hard moments?
options: Get through difficult moments and find friends.

questions.stem: Which use of a smile is mentioned?
options: To greet, apologise or ask for help.

questions.stem: What can a warm smile break down?
What does the speaker suggest doing when you feel down?
options: Try smiling, and you may feel better.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Learning Silent Acting
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: How are your acting classes going? I heard you act without speaking.

transcript.speaker: Sara
transcript.text: They're hard! We have to show feelings using only our faces and hands.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: That does sound difficult. Can people guess what you mean?

transcript.speaker: Sara
transcript.text: Sometimes. Last week I tried to show "I'm tired", but they thought I was sad.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Well, tired and sad can look quite similar.

transcript.speaker: Sara
transcript.text: True. I'm still not very confident about my silent acting.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Don't give up. It's good you tried — it takes practice.

transcript.speaker: Sara
transcript.text: Thanks. I'll keep practising and watch real people more closely.

exercises.translation_cn: Ben 问 Sara 无声表演课怎么样;Sara 说很难,只能用脸和手表达感受;上周想演"我累了",观众却以为是"难过";Ben 说累和难过看起来确实相似;Sara 对自己的无声表演还不太自信;Ben 鼓励她别放弃、要多练;Sara 决定继续练习并多观察真人。

questions.stem: What is special about Sara's acting classes?
What does Sara use to show feelings?
What happened when Sara tried to show "I'm tired"?
How does Sara feel about her silent acting?
What does Ben tell Sara at the end?
options: It's good she tried; it takes practice.
Acting is a waste of time.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Reading a Classroom
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: As a teacher, I learn a lot just by watching my students' bodies.
When students lean forward and look up, I know they are interested.
When a student keeps looking at the clock, he is probably bored.
Students who cross their arms tightly may feel worried or afraid.
Their quiet body language tells me when to slow down or offer help.
exercises.translation_cn: 作为老师,我只看学生的身体就能了解很多;学生前倾抬头时,我知道他们感兴趣;学生总看钟,多半是无聊了;紧紧交叉双臂的学生可能感到担忧或害怕;这些安静的肢体语言告诉我何时该放慢节奏或提供帮助。

questions.stem: How does the teacher learn about students?
What shows that students are interested?
options: They lean forward and look up.

questions.stem: What does looking at the clock probably mean?
What may tightly crossed arms suggest?
What does the quiet body language help the teacher decide?
options: When to slow down or offer help.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Asking for Clarification
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You looked at your watch during my talk. What did you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Oh, sorry! I didn't mean to be rude. I was just checking the time.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. I thought it meant you were bored.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: In other words, my body sent the wrong message?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Exactly. Body language can be easy to misread.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: So next time I should explain, or just put my watch away.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That would help. Asking "what do you mean?" can clear things up too.

transcript.speaker: Jack
transcript.text: Good idea. It's better to ask than to guess wrongly.

exercises.translation_cn: Anna 问 Jack 演讲时看表是什么意思;Jack 道歉,说只是看时间、无意失礼;Anna 以为那表示无聊;Jack 说也就是他的身体传错了信息;Anna 说肢体语言容易被误读;Jack 决定下次解释或收起手表;Anna 说直接问"你什么意思"也能澄清;Jack 同意,问比猜错好。

questions.stem: What did Jack do during Anna's talk?
Why did Jack really look at his watch?
options: He was just checking the time.

questions.stem: What did Anna first think his action meant?
What does Anna say about body language?
options: It can be easy to misread.

questions.stem: What do they agree is a good way to clear things up?
options: Asking what the other person means.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Tips for Travellers
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here are a few simple tips about body language for travellers.
Remember that a friendly gesture at home may be rude in another country.
Before you use a gesture, watch how the local people behave.
Keep your eye contact polite, not too long and not too short.
When in doubt, a warm smile is welcome almost everywhere.
exercises.translation_cn: 给旅行者几条关于肢体语言的小贴士:记住在本国友好的手势在别国可能无礼;用手势前先观察当地人怎么做;眼神接触要适度,别太久也别太短;拿不准时,温暖的微笑几乎处处受欢迎。

questions.stem: Who are these tips for?

questions.stem: What should you do before using a gesture?
options: Make it as big as possible.
